百 means “one hundred” and can also mean “many,” “all,” or “various.” Its early form is disputed: proposals include a marked 白-like base and a combined 一+白 spelling; another account says 白 first wrote the numeral before 百 was differentiated.

The formation is disputed. One analysis treats 百 as an indicative graph, with a mark above a 白-like base indicating one hundred. Another reads a combined 一-plus-白 spelling and proposes that 白 was borrowed for the numeral because the words sounded alike or similar; it suggests the spelling later reduced to 百. A separate account calls 百 a “special phonetic” graph: 白 first wrote the numeral and supplied sound, and a dedicated 百 was later differentiated. That account also reads the Shang form as 白 with an added indicator, then describes lower 自 as a later corruption or change of 白. These proposals do not establish whether they describe different forms or stages.

In the combined-spelling analysis, 白 supplies a sound cue. A separate account proposes that 白 first wrote the numeral as a whole graph and also supplied sound in the later 百; it describes a later lower 自 as a change of 白. These claims do not settle the earliest lower form’s identity.

One account proposes that a combined 一百 spelling later became 百, possibly through omission of 一 in speech. A separate account calls 百 a “special phonetic” graph: 白 first wrote the numeral and supplied sound, before a dedicated 百 was differentiated. It reads the Shang form as 白 with an added indicator and describes a later lower 自 as a corruption or change of 白.
